Bots with faces, names, and a memory of their own.

Hexbot runs a handful of bots on your own Mac, Linux box, or home server. Each one keeps its own notes, works with the model provider you choose, and joins rooms with the people in your house.

Read the install guideHow it works
KitchenA room with Scout, Ledger, and you
You@Scout what did we decide about the trip last month?
ScoutThe second week of October, the cabin by the lake. Ledger has the deposit receipt from the 14th.
LedgerDeposit was 320 from the shared card. The balance is due two weeks before you leave.
+Message Kitchen

Scout answered from the memory it kept of a chat four weeks earlier. Ledger joined because it was named. Neither one needed you to explain the trip again.

Memory that lasts

Every conversation stays until you archive it. Each bot keeps private notes and a searchable history, and a shared core memory holds what all your bots should know. Overnight, bots dream over the day and keep what mattered.

Rooms for people and bots

Put several bots and several people in one chat. Mention a bot to bring it in, or pick a main bot that answers when nobody is named. Bots can message each other, and you can watch the whole exchange.

Runs where you say

The daemon lives on one machine and keeps working when the app is closed. Pair a phone or a second laptop with a short code on your network, over Tailscale, or through Hexbot Connect when you are away.

Your data stays on your hardware.

Conversations, memory, files, and provider keys live in ~/.hexbot on the machine running the daemon. Bring your own API key or a subscription you already pay for.

  • ApprovalsTools run only when you say so. Auto mode lets a small model wave through the low-risk ones.
  • Devices you can revokeEvery paired phone and laptop appears in settings with a revoke button.
  • Delete means deleteRemoving a conversation also removes the memory a bot took from it.
  • Connect stays out of the wayHexbot Connect brokers your identity and a hostname. Chat traffic never passes through it.
  • Open sourceAGPL-3.0. Read it, fork it, run it yourself.
